description: IPC for the bundled UI window only. No remote origin is listed, so remote content gets no IPC at all. The HTTP plugin's scope is NOT here: it is granted at runtime for the connected deployment's origin only (see http_scope.rs). The opener hands only https and loopback http to the system browser (the scope is a glob: `[[]`/`[]]` are literal brackets, and any http URL with userinfo is denied so `http://localhost:x@host` cannot pass as loopback). The webview may listen to (never emit) events: `agent://event` and `app://command` arrive through `plugin:event|listen`, which the ACL refuses without `core:event:allow-listen`. The two window permissions are what `data-tauri-drag-region` needs (drag, double-click to zoom) under the macOS overlay title bar; `core:window:allow-set-theme` lets the UI make the native window (and its sidebar material) follow the app's light/dark mode; `log:allow-log` lets the UI write its errors and diagnostics to the host's log file (it cannot read it); the notification and window-state plugins are driven from Rust and get no webview permission.
